title: Quantitative Methods
source: Carte mentale — séries temporelles & recherche quantitative énergie
subtitle: Four commodity-desk situations on synthetic data — power prices and the weather, the diesel crack, what the crude desk knew and when, and Brent vs WTI — each one a trader's question that needs data work, statistics and a desk-level answer

projects.title: Weather, load and day-ahead power prices: cold and still, or something else?
projects.question: “We had several very high day-ahead electricity prices during cold, low-wind periods. Can you investigate whether weather and renewable generation explain these price spikes, or whether something else is happening?”
projects.commodity: a fictional Central-European power market, three zones (CET/CEST), hourly 2023–2024; gas price
projects.data_focus: local time vs UTC and DST days, duplicates vs revisions, structural vs failed gaps, a stale daily state, irregular weather observations, zone groupby, average MW vs MWh
projects.data: p1_power_hourly_vendor · p1_zone_load_hourly · p1_zone_temperature_obs · p1_zones_reference · p1_weather_normals (all synthetic)

projects.title: Diesel cracks, refinery disruptions and extreme observations
projects.question: “The diesel crack has widened materially. Is this consistent with tighter physical supply, or are we looking at a data problem or a misleading statistical relationship?”
projects.commodity: ICE Gasoil, NY Harbor ULSD, RBOB, jet, Brent (daily 2017–2023); European imports, refinery outages, distillate stocks (monthly)
projects.data_focus: a long vendor file with mixed units (USD/t, USc/gal, USD/gal), duplicate keys, a frozen feed, unit errors and impossible prints, genuine zeros vs non-reporting, events to months
projects.data: p2_products_daily_long · p2_market_events · p2_diesel_imports_monthly · p2_refinery_outages · p2_distillate_fundamentals_monthly (all synthetic)

projects.title: What did the desk actually know at the time?
projects.question: “Can we use weekly stock reports and monthly demand data to understand WTI price reactions? I need to know what information was available when the market moved, not what the database says today.”
projects.commodity: WTI (daily settlements and release-time snapshots), US crude stocks (weekly, with consensus), US oil demand (monthly vintages), 2019–2024
projects.data_focus: five timestamps, release calendar and delays, New York vs UTC, backfilled records, backward as-of joins on availability, vintages, truncation tests, purged labels
projects.data: p3_us_crude_stocks_weekly · p3_wti_daily · p3_wti_release_snapshots · p3_us_oil_demand_vintages · p3_release_events · p3_decision_table_daily (all synthetic)

projects.title: Brent, WTI and the difference between a statistical relationship and an economic one
projects.question: “Brent and WTI often move together. Can we establish whether this is a meaningful relationship, or are we simply correlating two trending price series?”
projects.commodity: Brent, WTI (daily 2012–2019, end of the US export ban), an unrelated coffee price, US diesel demand (monthly 2010–2019)
projects.data_focus: a clean research panel: the work is choosing transformations, deterministic terms and tests — and knowing what each result does not show

retired_note: Exercises of the previous version with no successor (crude dataset building, SQLite, lead-lag, model selection). Their progress stays in data/progress.json; the old track is archived in archive/quant-v2/.
